1. Always follow the project's coding standards and guidelines when writing code.
2. Use proper folder structure and file organization to maintain a clean and manageable codebase.
2. Follow frontend best practices while making changes or generating new code.
3. Ensure that the code is well-structured, maintainable, and follows best practices and try to write clean, readable code with low cognitive complexity.
4. Write meaningful and descriptive comments where necessary to explain complex logic or decisions.
5. Optimize code for performance without sacrificing readability and maintainability.
6. Ensure proper error handling and validation to prevent unexpected behavior and improve code robustness.
7. Write unit tests and integration tests to verify the correctness and reliability of the code.
8. Keep dependencies up-to-date and avoid introducing unnecessary or outdated libraries.
9. Follow accessibility best practices to ensure the application is usable by all users.
10. Regularly review and refactor code to maintain high code quality and reduce technical debt.
